description: Maximize the minimum altitude among triangles in a triangulation of a strictly convex polygon.

source.title: Encyclopedia of Algorithms, DOI 715: Max-Min Triangle Height Triangulation
source.reference: Tan's Encyclopedia chapter summarizes max-min height; the edge-insertion method follows the cited triangulation paper.
source.edge_insertion_reference: M. Bern, H. Edelsbrunner, D. Eppstein, S. Mitchell, and T. S. Tan, Edge insertion for optimal triangulations (1993).
source.algorithm_attribution: Deterministic edge insertion with optimal subpolygon retriangulation; clean-room bounded adaptation.
source.implementation_status: Clean-room implementations based on the published objective and algorithm description; no source code copied.

polygon_requirements: vertices listed in strict counterclockwise boundary order

output.encoding: reduced_num*513 + reduced_den for the maximum achievable minimum squared altitude

contract.primary_objective: maximize the minimum squared altitude over all triangles of a triangulation
contract.tie_refinement: Among triangulations with equal minimum squared altitude, prefer fewer triangles attaining that minimum. This only makes edge-insertion choices deterministic; it does not change the primary max-min result.
contract.exact_arithmetic: All scores are reduced rational numbers and compared by integer cross multiplication.
contract.edge_order: Scan absent non-boundary diagonals in lexicographic endpoint order; accept the first strict improvement of (minimum score, count attaining minimum), then restart.
contract.subpolygon_retriangulation: Dynamic programming chooses the lexicographically first split among equal refined objectives.
contract.improvement_limit_reason: With at most five vertices there are at most ten possible triangle scores, each paired with a minimum-triangle count from one through three; each accepted step strictly advances among at most thirty such pairs.

complexity.time: Bounded by the fixed five-vertex state space; each subpolygon DP and edge-insertion pass uses constant-sized tables.
complexity.auxiliary_space: O(n^2) for the doubled cyclic subpolygon table, with n<=5.
